3. During pendency of the suit plaintiff filed an application under Section 24 of the Code  of Civil Procedure to the Court of the learned District Judge, Jamalpur registered as Miscellaneous Case No.32 of 1992 for transfer of the said case to another Court which was allowed and the case was transferred to the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, numbering the suit as Title Suit No.43 of 1992. The teamed Subordinate Judge rejected the application for injunction on 09.11.1992 on contest. Plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.46 of 1992 in the Court of the learned District Judge which was rejected by him on 06.02.1993. Plaintiff filed Civil Revision. No. 692 of 1993 in the High Court Division and obtained it Rule which was discharged on 06.11.2002 directing the trial Court to dispose .of the suit within 4 (four) months. Plaintiff filed an application to the trial Court on 12.01.2004 for mandatory injunction against the defendants alleging her dispossession by them. Trial Court passed an order directing the parties to lead evidence on the said application on dispossession vide order dated 07.06.2004. Defendant- petitioner filed Civil Revision No.24 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Jamalpur which was allowed setting aside the order of the trial Court directing to dispose of the suit within 2(two) months. 

 4. Accordingly date was fixed for peremptory hearing of the suit. P. W. I deposed in part on 23.11.2005 and filed another application under Section 24 of the Code to the learned District Judge for transfer of the case to another Court which was allowed on 28.06.2006 and the case was transferred to the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jamalpur and renumbered as Title Suit No.18 of 2006 to try and dispose of the suit. 

 5. Plaintiff examined 3 P. Ws. including herself as P. W.1 and the defendants examined 5 D. Ws which was closed on 27.09.2006 and the case was fixed for argument on 11.10.2006. On 11.10,2006 the plaintiff filed an application for recalling P.W.1 which was disallowed by the trial Court. On the same day defendants filed an application for further evidence and the plaintiff again filed an application for recalling P. W.1 Trial Court allowed both the applications on consent of both the parties fixing 13.11.2006 for further evidence. On 13.11.2006 defendants examined 3 witnesses. D. Ws. 6-8. 

 6. P. W.1 was examined and cross-examined on 14.11.2006 on recall and trial Court fixed 27.11.06 for argument. Defendants completed their submissions on 07.02.2007 when plaintiff filed another application under Section 24 of the Code registered as Miscellaneous Case No.2 of 2007 for transfer of the suit and the learned District Judge allowed the application transferring the case to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, Jamalpur on 04.04.2007. The plaintiff filed an, application on 17.05.2007 for further recalling of P.W.1 and the learned Additional District Judge vide his impugned Order No.90 dated 30.05.2007 allowed the same. Hence this Rule at the instance of the defendant- petitioners. 

 7. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners criticized the impugned order as a total non-speaking order submitting that the same has been passed without assigning any reason whatsoever and erroneously relying on a decision mentioned in the order. He contends that under Order 18 rule 17 of the Code, a Court has ample power to recall any witness only to remove ambiguity and to pass a proper judgment, but the trial Court allowed the application for recall for the second time without finding, such necessity and as such the impugned order is liable to be set aside. He continued that earlier application dated 11.10.2006 filed by the plaintiff for recalling P.W.1 and the subsequent application filed on 17.05.2007 for recalling same P.W. 1 are on the same and identical matters except documents/ papers mentioned in paragraphs (d) and (e) of the subsequent application and as such the trial Court committed serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in allowing the second application to fill up the lacuna of plaintiff's case. Mr. Amin also argued that the documents mentioned in paragraphs (d) and (e) of the subsequent application dated 17.05.2007 were already within the knowledge and possession of the plaintiff but those were not put to P. W. 1 during her examination earlier and as such cannot be allowed to fill up the lacuna of plaintiff's case and that those use also not at all necessary for disposal of the suit. In support of his submission Mr. Amin has cited a decision in the case of Nurul Islam Vs. Md. Abdur Rashid & ors., reported in 37 DLR (AD) 32. He also referred the decision in the case of Morsalin (Md). and others Vs. Nurul Huda and others, reported in 48 DLR (HCD) 593 relied by the Courts below in passing the impugned order. 

 8. On the other hand Mr. Md. Maqbul Ahmed Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party no. 1 submitted that while deposing on recall on 14,11.2006 P. W. 1 in her examination-in-chief made some statement in respect of certain documents as well as in her cross-examination but those were not marked as exhibits by the trial Court and as such recall of P. W. 1 is necessary for making those documents as exhibits otherwise the plaintiff shall be highly prejudiced. Mr. Chowdhury further contends that the trial Court did not commit any error of law in recalling the P. W. 1 for the second time and examination of P. W. 1 on recall for the second time is also not to fill up the lacuna of her case but only to fill up the omission and mistake committed by the Court as well as by the learned Advocate in not marking those documents as exhibits in accordance with law of evidence in order to use those documents for writing a proper judgment. He further submits that the documents mentions in the subsequent application for recalling P. W. 1 are not new documents, rather same and identical with the documents mentioned and submitted to Court with the earlier application by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, etc Mr. Chowdhury relied on the decision reported in 48 DLR 593 referred by the trial Court in it's impugned judgment.9. Perused the impugned order and heard the learned Advocates of both the sides. 10. At the time of making submission Mr. Chowdhury read out the deposition of P.W.1 made on recall on 14.11.2006 from the certified copy. P.W.1 on recall clearly deposed that the defendants took attempts to dispossess her from the  suit land on 26.06.1992, she got an order of status quo on 18.07.1992, her father died of cancer on 01.04.1993, etc. She further deposed in her chief that one Fazlur Rahman and Rishi sworn an affidavit on 03.08.1992. She was extensively and exhaustingly cross-examined by the learned Advocate for the defendants where in her statement in cross-, examination she also mentioned about the above incident and documents firmly denying the defence suggestions. 

 12. From reading of the application Mr. Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing. for the petitioners submitted and Mr. Maqbul Ahmed Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party also conceded that the documents mentioned in both the applications are more or less similar and identical except paragraphs (d) and (e) of the subsequent application which are relating to the criminal cases. 

 15. In the instant case recall of P. W. 1 is necessary to comply the law of evidence to mark the documents as exhibits referred by I the witness in her statement made before the Court but omitted either by the lapse of the Court or by her learned Advocate. This is not a matter to fill up any lacuna of plaintiff's case, but a bona fide requirement to fill up the aforesaid omission. In such view of the matter I find no merit in the Rule which is liable to be discharged. 16.1n the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. , 17. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated. 18. Let a copy of this order be sent to the concern Court below at once.
